India's biggest names fell twenty to thirty percent in one year. This quiet stock made one hundred forty five.
Say you put one lakh rupees in each of them, on the third of November last year.
Reliance? Seventy nine thousand today. HDFC Bank? Seventy thousand. Infosys? Eighty thousand.
But the fourth one... turned the same one lakh into two lakh forty five thousand.
Its name is Laurus Labs. A medicine maker from Hyderabad. No ads. No famous brand.
So what did it have? Last quarter, its revenue grew thirty three percent. Its profit more than doubled.
Meanwhile, Infosys cut its growth target to just one to two percent. And HDFC Bank's margins shrank, while it changed its CEO.
Here's the lesson. The market doesn't pay for big names. It pays for growth. But after a run this big, even experts disagree. Kotak still rates it a sell.
